items.title: Ernie Cagnolatti Interview, 1961-04-05
items.q: He was a tap dancer. He was a Bill Robinson.

ctx.x: One of the things I call him, Uncle Alan, see we come up with the, his mom and all together, he used to try to play clarinet too when he was small. But he could dance.
Oh yeah, he was a tap dancer. He was a Bill Robinson.

He was a musical and clarinet. And sing like King Cole. When I went to the opera house. But couldn't play harmonica. When I went to the opera house, he said, you don't have no drum. He said, no, you ain't. Got last that drum, you can't come from here. I said, okay, I bought a, that white set big footbill hat and put him on it. Well, he tore, boy, the street from Jersey. Every night he, every night he's getting better.
